title: Chain the Board paging beside the Side panel journey through fluent page objects

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-300#chain-board-paging-side-panel-page-objects at 936e450f23f48e0916a54b5a91ff1bf1bb95e78b

Verdict: Caught. This applies only to the Recently-done-count fault on the observed path.

Promise checked: a session is started from the ready Backlog card (Story B) while the Board is paged back to Backlog beside the side panel. After that, the card shows exactly one session, the view stays at Backlog+Taken, and the right control still reads "Recently done 0 entries".

Fault chosen and checked against dashboard/src: dashboard/src/Board.tsx, in the useRecentlyDone call. The `records` argument was changed from `sessions.done` to `[...sessions.done, ...work.backlog.flatMap(({identity}) => storyCardSessionsOf(launches.records, sourceId, identity))]`. This counts a Backlog story's open sessions into Recently done. The caller suggested this fault. No fixture or assertion was changed.

Maintained check examined: dashboard/frontend-tests/navigation/board-paging-side-panel.spec.ts, second test ("paged back to Backlog beside the side panel, a session started ..."). The final `board.shows(["Backlog","Taken"], ["Recently done 0 entries"])` caught the fault. It is at spec line 94 and goes through FrontendBoard.shows (dashboard/tests/support/frontendBoard.ts:51) to expectView (dashboard/tests/boardPage.ts:49), whose columnPagingControls toHaveText failed: expected "Recently done 0 entries", received "Recently done 1 entry". The earlier `board.showsBacklogCardSessions(readyStory, 1)` passed, so the card still held its one session.

Runs (scratch worktree from the selected revision, pinned node v24.21.0, npm ci; focused command run with the strict silent reporter; each run rebuilds the app):
- Baseline: exit 0. The proof record (OPEN_DOUGH_DASHBOARD_FRONTEND_PROOF_RECORD) shows both tests ran and passed, selectedCount 2, phase completed. This confirms reach.
- Fault: exit 1. Test 1 passed. Test 2 failed at the final shows, as quoted above.
- Independent witness: a scratch copy of the spec, with the maintained final assertions replaced by plain reads, under the same fault. After the start, the only paging control read "Recently done 1 entry" and `--leftmost` stayed 0. Paging to Recently done showed its column listing "Story B / SEED-B#b / Working / Claude Code": the newly started open session was wrongly listed as recently done. So the wrong behavior was observed directly on the intended path.
- Restored: both edits reverted with git checkout. `git status --porcelain` matched the empty pre-probe record at HEAD 936e450f2. The rerun of the same command exited 0, both tests passed and the proof record phase was completed. The scratch worktree was then removed.

Side observation on the paging fault (not part of the verdict):
- I first tried a Board.tsx effect that calls move(1) when launches.records grows. Scratch console logs showed it fired: leftmost went to 1. But the product's focus return to the Backlog card, after the start dialog closed, moved the view back to 0 straight away. The spec passed, and the promised view held, so there was nothing to catch.
- A variant that delays move(1) by 300 ms did move the view to Taken+Recently done ("Backlog 2 entries" control, leftmost 1). It did so only after the test's final assertion had already passed and the test had ended. The maintained spec passed.
- So the spec checks the view right after untilPageRequestsAnswered. It does not observe whether the view stays later. This came from a timer-based scratch fault, so it is recorded as context, not as a verdict. Any finite check can be outrun by a longer delay.

Next proof action: none needed for the Recently-done-count promise. If the caller wants the "view stays" half covered against late moves, that is a separate decision.

Prior disposition: the coordinator had already seen that changing the expected numbers in the spec makes it fail. This probe adds a product-side fault catch and does not depend on that observation.

Cost:
- Test runtime (measured, Playwright per-test durationMs from the proof records): baseline 1410 ms + 1102 ms; fault run 1703 ms + 6495 ms (failed test, including its 5 s expect timeout); restored 1413 ms + 822 ms. Restored focused command wall time, including the app build: 3415 ms (measured with the host clock). Machine load average was about 4.3-6.
- Human effort: unavailable. No separate human-time measure was recorded for this invocation.
- Agent effort: unavailable. No token or turn meter is available to this agent.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 214475 ms (measured), from 1794973820870 to 1794974035345 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: checked revision 936e450f23f48e0916a54b5a91ff1bf1bb95e78b, verdict Caught, no follow-up. The late-move side observation concerns the spec's unchanged settle-then-check timing, which this refactor kept as it was.
